title: Change Conversations software and contracts
summary: Modify the Conversations library, CLI, App Server compatibility, normalization, packaging, tests, or documentation.
use_when: Conversations code, tests, protocol behavior, public schema, Chancery contract, packaging, release workflow, or documentation is being changed.
do_not_use_when: The request is ordinary use of the installed Conversations CLI.
Only release publication or deployment outside a submitted CI job is requested.
outcome: A minimal tested Conversations change with matching public and operational documentation. Storage access remains limited to App Server.
effects: Modifies Conversations source, tests, documentation, packaging, or authored contracts.
A public-schema or compatibility change can affect local consumers of the Conversations Rust library and JSON output.
CI submission authorizes manager integration, validation, bounded repair, deployment, and the outcome email. Release publication remains separate.
authority: Conversations owns its typed normalized schema, CLI, filters, deduplication, and packaging.
Codex App Server remains the sole authority for conversation discovery and storage compatibility.
No implementation shortcut may create raw JSONL or SQLite coupling.
success: The changed code and affected documents agree.
Fake App Server tests cover every affected protocol and normalization boundary.
Process-lifecycle tests prove descendant cleanup remains scoped to the private launch group when that boundary changes.
Submit the committed change with `./ci.sh submit COMMIT` from the Cell root and verify the retained manager job outcome.
failure_and_recovery: Do not turn incomplete App Server data into a successful partial corpus.
Preserve the legacy fallback only for unavailable turn pagination, not arbitrary read errors.
Packaging changes retain content identity, tamper detection, prior selectors, and post-switch rollback.
privacy: Fixtures must be synthetic; release bundles must never contain real transcript data.
Diagnostics and JSON examples should avoid private paths and conversation text.
steps: Read `AGENTS.md` and the exact architecture, CLI, installation, and Chancery documents for the changed behavior.
Consult the current official Codex App Server documentation before changing protocol assumptions.
Implement the smallest change with synthetic App Server fixtures and update shared contracts in the same change.

Commit the change, submit it with `./ci.sh submit COMMIT` from the Cell root, and verify the retained manager job outcome. Release publication and deployment outside that job require separate authority.
checkpoints: No code reads Codex JSONL or SQLite files.
Default output remains user/assistant-only, root-task-only, active-and-archived, and state-database-only.
Turn and thread pagination, copied-item deduplication, and incomplete-read failure remain proved.
The retained manager job records passing validation and the deployment and notification outcomes; release publication remains separate.
adaptation: Regenerate or consult the version-matched App Server schema when a documented method or field differs across installed Codex versions.
Scale fake-server coverage to the changed boundary without adding a raw-storage fallback.
stop_when: The desired data is unavailable through the documented App Server API.
A public-schema change would silently break an existing local library consumer.
The change would require task mutation, a persistent index, or raw Codex storage access outside the approved product boundary.
does_not_authorize: Running `release.sh`, which commits, tags, and pushes.
Deploying an installed Conversations release outside the submitted manager job.
Mutating Codex tasks or accessing private Codex storage directly.

consumers.statement: An interactive developer authorized to change the Conversations repository may use this operation for its library, CLI, typed schema, App Server compatibility, tests, packaging, or documentation.

Ordinary history exploration, task mutation, release publication, deployment outside the submitted manager job, raw Codex storage access, daemon or index creation, and model interpretation are outside this operation.

preconditions.statement: The developer has current Conversations source, applicable Semantics and installed contract context, exact architecture, CLI, installation and Chancery documents, and authority for the requested change.
A protocol assumption change is grounded in current official version-matched Codex App Server documentation and preserves or explicitly versions the public typed boundary.

inputs.statement: Inputs are the requested scoped change, current library and CLI source, synthetic fake-App-Server fixtures, product documents, installed capability contracts, and any authorized compatibility or recovery constraints.
Real transcript fixtures, raw JSONL or SQLite inspection, inferred private storage formats, task mutation, and arbitrary unsupported App Server fields are not acceptable inputs.

outputs.statement: The output is a minimal source and documentation change with a verified retained CI manager outcome. Synthetic product tests cover the affected protocol, normalization, lifecycle, compatibility, packaging, and rollback behavior.
This operation does not publish, tag, push, deploy outside the submitted manager job, refresh metadata, retrieve a private corpus, or mutate a Codex task.

data_semantics.statement: Changes preserve App Server as the only discovery and storage-compatibility authority and Conversations as owner of typed normalization, filters, stable references, deduplication, and failure-on-incomplete behavior.
The default public corpus remains user-and-assistant-only, root-task-only, active-and-archived, and state-database-only unless an incompatible versioned contract explicitly changes it.

identity_and_units.statement: Conversations package and provider release, entry contract version, typed JSON schema, host, thread, turn and item references, Codex CLI version, and App Server protocol evolve as distinct identities.
The development operation publishes no effort, cost, schedule, or accounting unit.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Completion requires the smallest owning code and every affected CLI, architecture, installation and Chancery document to agree, with synthetic fixtures covering the exact protocol and normalization boundary and a verified retained manager job outcome.
Process-lifecycle changes prove private-group descendant cleanup, and packaging changes prove content identity, tamper detection, retained selectors, and rollback as applicable.
Passing source tests alone does not establish a released, deployed, runtime-compatible, metadata-refreshed, or complete live App Server result.

access.statement: The operation uses the interactive developer's authorized local filesystem and shell for scoped Conversations repository work and synthetic local test processes. CI submission uses the installed manager for bounded Nucleus repair, deployment, and the outcome email. Repair may read candidate source and diagnostics; the outcome email contains job metadata.
It grants no private Codex storage, real transcript, task mutation, Codex authentication, release publication, installed deployment outside the submitted manager job, or unrelated process authority.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Changes preserve one short-lived App Server process group per invocation, complete pagination or explicit failure, the narrow method-unavailable fallback, stable typed references, and no retained Conversations service state.
Incompatible public schemas or packaging behavior are versioned and tested rather than silently changing existing local library or JSON consumers.

operational_limits.statement: The operation is limited to the smallest Conversations-owned change and stops when required data is absent from App Server, a local consumer would silently break, or the change requires task mutation, persistent indexing, or raw storage.
No development duration, review turnaround, release cadence, future App Server support window, or deployment schedule is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Development contract version 3 requires synthetic version-matched App Server proof, explicit public-schema compatibility, synchronized exact documentation, and content-addressed packaging rollback.
CI submission includes the manager deployment and outcome email. Release publication and installed deployment outside that job remain separately authorized operations.
No perpetual support window or deprecation period for Conversations, Codex CLI, or App Server versions is promised.

reliances.statement: Changes to public query or normalization behavior rely on Conversations' exact history-exploration contract as the owning product promise.
Protocol and compatibility changes rely on Codex App Server's documented behavior, but no dedicated installed Chancery contract describes that upstream promise.
Conversations development relies on its registered Semantics repository for maintained project terminology while source, tests, and product documentation remain authoritative for behavior.
